onb.title: Welcome to NET Sniffer
onb.subtitle: See every device on your network, keep it secure and know when something changes.
onb.f1_d: IP, MAC, vendor, model and type for everything connected.
onb.f2_d: Find weak Wi-Fi settings and risky open services.
onb.f3_d: Download, upload, latency and jitter with history.
onb.f4_d: New devices, outages and security issues in real time.
onb.legal_t: Use it on networks you own or manage
onb.legal_d: NET Sniffer only uses standard discovery protocols and connection checks. Scanning networks you don't have permission to inspect may be illegal.
onb.accept: I will only use NET Sniffer on networks that I own or am authorized to administer.

security.title: Security audit
security.intro: Check your Wi-Fi, router and every device for risky configurations.
security.intro_long: The audit checks Wi-Fi encryption, UPnP exposure, router administration and the services every online device exposes. It takes about a minute.
security.no_findings_d: Great job — nothing to fix right now.
security.ethics_d: Checks only detect what is exposed. Nothing is exploited, no passwords are tried and no traffic is intercepted.

pass.upnp_disabled: UPnP port mapping is not exposed by the router
pass.all_trusted: Every device on the network is recognized

wifi_open.title: Wi-Fi “{ssid}” is open
wifi_open.desc: Anyone nearby can join and see unencrypted traffic.
wifi_open.fix: In your router's Wi-Fi settings enable WPA3-Personal (or WPA2/WPA3 mixed) with a strong passphrase.

wifi_wep.title: Wi-Fi “{ssid}” uses WEP
wifi_wep.desc: WEP can be cracked in minutes.
wifi_wep.fix: Switch to WPA3-Personal or at least WPA2-AES in the router settings.

wifi_wpa.title: Wi-Fi “{ssid}” uses legacy WPA
wifi_wpa.desc: The original WPA/TKIP is obsolete and vulnerable.

wifi_wpa2.title: Wi-Fi “{ssid}” uses WPA2
wifi_wpa2.desc: WPA2 is still acceptable, but WPA3 resists offline password guessing.
wifi_wpa2.fix: If all your devices support it, enable WPA3 or WPA2/WPA3 transition mode. Use a passphrase of 12+ characters.

wifi_tkip.title: Wi-Fi uses TKIP encryption
wifi_tkip.fix: Select AES/CCMP only in the router's wireless security settings.

upnp_enabled.title: UPnP enabled on router {router}
upnp_enabled.desc: Any device or malware on your network can open ports to the internet automatically.
upnp_enabled.fix: Disable UPnP in the router unless a game console or app really needs it; forward specific ports manually instead.

router_http.title: Router admin page without HTTPS
router_http.desc: {device} ({ip}) serves its administration page over unencrypted HTTP.
router_http.fix: Enable HTTPS administration if available, use a strong admin password and disable remote (WAN) administration.

untrusted_devices.title: {count} unrecognized devices online
untrusted_devices.fix: Open each device, confirm you know it and mark it as trusted. Block anything you don't recognize and change your Wi-Fi password.

cameras_present.title: {count} cameras on the network
cameras_present.fix: Make sure you know every camera, update their firmware and change default passwords.

port_telnet.title: Telnet open on {device}
port_telnet.desc: Telnet (port {port}) sends passwords in clear text and is a favorite target of IoT botnets.
port_telnet.fix: Disable Telnet in the device settings or firmware; use SSH if remote shell access is needed.

port_ftp.title: FTP open on {device}
port_ftp.desc: FTP (port {port}) transmits credentials and files unencrypted.
port_ftp.fix: Disable FTP or replace it with SFTP/FTPS.

port_tftp.title: TFTP open on {device}
port_tftp.desc: TFTP has no authentication at all.
port_tftp.fix: Disable TFTP when not provisioning devices.

port_smb.title: File sharing (SMB) on {device}
port_smb.desc: Port {port} is open. Fine for computers and NAS that share files, unexpected on other devices.
port_smb.fix: Disable file sharing if unused, keep SMBv1 disabled and protect shares with passwords.

port_msrpc.title: Windows RPC exposed on {device}
port_msrpc.desc: Port {port} is normal on Windows PCs on a private network.
port_msrpc.fix: Keep Windows updated and set this network as Private only if you trust it.

port_rdp.title: Remote Desktop open on {device}
port_rdp.desc: RDP (port {port}) is a frequent attack target.
port_rdp.fix: Disable Remote Desktop if not used, require Network Level Authentication and never forward it to the internet.

port_vnc.title: VNC open on {device}
port_vnc.desc: VNC (port {port}) often uses weak or no authentication.
port_vnc.fix: Disable VNC or protect it with a strong password and only allow it through a VPN.

port_docker.title: Docker API exposed on {device}
port_docker.desc: Port {port} gives full control of the host without authentication.
port_docker.fix: Bind the Docker daemon to a Unix socket only or enable TLS client authentication (port 2376).

port_adb.title: Android debugging (ADB) open on {device}
port_adb.desc: ADB over network (port {port}) allows full control of the Android device.
port_adb.fix: Turn off “Wireless debugging/ADB over network” in Developer options.

port_mqtt.title: Unencrypted MQTT on {device}
port_mqtt.desc: MQTT (port {port}) controls smart-home devices and may allow anonymous access.
port_mqtt.fix: Require username/password and prefer MQTT over TLS (port 8883).

port_rtsp.title: Video stream (RTSP) on {device}
port_rtsp.desc: RTSP (port {port}) can expose live camera video.
port_rtsp.fix: Set a strong camera password, update firmware and disable RTSP if you only use the vendor app.

port_database.title: Database {service} exposed on {device}
port_database.desc: Port {port} is reachable from the whole network.
port_database.fix: Bind the database to localhost or restrict it with a firewall, and require authentication.

port_x11.title: X11 display server open on {device}
port_x11.desc: Port {port} may allow capturing the screen and keystrokes.
port_x11.fix: Disable TCP listening for X11 (use -nolisten tcp).

port_rpcbind.title: RPCbind open on {device}
port_rpcbind.desc: Port {port} reveals RPC services and is abused in attacks.
port_rpcbind.fix: Disable rpcbind if NFS is not used.

port_proxy.title: Open proxy on {device}
port_proxy.desc: A SOCKS proxy on port {port} can relay traffic.
port_proxy.fix: Disable the proxy or require authentication.

port_modbus.title: Modbus open on {device}
port_modbus.desc: Industrial protocol on port {port} without authentication.
port_modbus.fix: Isolate the device on a separate network segment.

port_dvr.title: DVR/NVR service on {device}
port_dvr.desc: Port {port} belongs to a video recorder protocol known for vulnerabilities.
port_dvr.fix: Update firmware, change default passwords and never expose it to the internet.

port_suspicious.title: Unusual service on {device}
port_suspicious.desc: Port {port} is commonly used by backdoors and test tools.
port_suspicious.fix: Check which program listens on this port and remove it if unknown.

port_webmin.title: Webmin on {device}
port_webmin.fix: Keep it updated and restrict access to trusted hosts.

port_tr069.title: TR-069 management on {device}
port_tr069.desc: Remote management port {port} used by ISPs.
port_tr069.fix: Normal on ISP routers; ensure it isn't reachable from your LAN devices if not required.

port_rsync.title: rsync open on {device}
port_rsync.desc: Port {port} may allow unauthenticated file access.
port_rsync.fix: Require authentication or disable the daemon.

port_nfs.title: NFS open on {device}
port_nfs.desc: Port {port} shares folders over the network.
port_nfs.fix: Restrict exports to specific hosts and disable if unused.

port_mail_plain.title: Unencrypted mail service on {device}
port_mail_plain.desc: {service} on port {port} sends credentials in clear text.

port_winrm.title: WinRM on {device}
port_winrm.fix: Disable if unused or restrict to administrators.

cams.title: Hidden camera finder
cams.subtitle: ONVIF, RTSP, DVR services and vendor fingerprints
cams.hint: Searches every online device for signs of a camera or video recorder.
cams.none_d: {count} devices checked. Phones and laptops can still have built-in cameras.
cams.advice: Recognize every camera? If not, check where it is physically and block it from the device panel.

parental.periods_hint: Internet is blocked inside each period. A period that ends before it starts continues past midnight.

parental.quick_pause_d: One tap to pause a device for an hour
parental.need_backend: Connect your router to enforce blocking
parental.need_backend_d: Blocking is applied by your own router. Configure the connection once in Settings.
parental.backend_error: The router rejected the last change

block.guide_desc: NET Sniffer blocks devices through your router's own administration interface — the legitimate way, with your admin credentials.
block.none_d: Choose how NET Sniffer talks to your router.
block.backend_ssh_d: OpenWrt, GL.iNet, Turris, DD-WRT and other Linux routers. Adds the device MAC to a firewall drop list.
block.backend_fritz_d: Uses the official TR-064 interface (enable “Allow access for applications” in the FRITZ!Box).
block.backend_local_d: For a Raspberry Pi or Linux box acting as router/hotspot. Requires root.
block.manual_d: Add this MAC address to the block list / MAC filter in your router's admin page:
block.intro: Device blocking and parental controls are enforced by your router. Credentials are stored encrypted on this device and used only to talk to your router.
block.legal: The router's SSH host key is pinned on first connection. NET Sniffer never impersonates other devices on the network.

settings.n_internet_d: Alert when the connection drops and recovers.
settings.n_security_d: Alert on audit issues and detected cameras.
settings.n_push_d: Use any combination of ntfy, Telegram or a webhook.
settings.remote_enable_d: Serve NET Sniffer to your phone and other computers on this network. Set a password first.
settings.remote_password_d: Required to open NET Sniffer from other devices.
settings.remote_hint: Scan the QR code from a device on the same Wi-Fi. For access away from home use a VPN (WireGuard, Tailscale) instead of opening router ports.
settings.remote_headless: Running in server mode — remote access is always on and protected by your password.
settings.public_ip_d: Ask Cloudflare for your public IP and ISP name.
settings.clear_alerts_d: Delete all alerts and device activity.
settings.logout_d: End the session on this browser.
settings.legal: NET Sniffer is intended for monitoring and securing networks that you own or are authorized to administer. It uses standard discovery protocols and connection checks only.
settings.oss: Built with Python, FastAPI, zeroconf, psutil, httpx, pywebview and other open-source software. MAC vendor data © IEEE Registration Authority.
